adjudication.procedure: Post-score review of every design with newly high-confidence false pairs. Same operator inspected original PDF crops, pinned CAD symbol definitions, truth and all three saved predictions. This was not independent blinded adjudication. No extractor, truth or threshold was changed.
adjudication.reference_comparison: No new cases versus recent baseline: all 126 complete candidate predictions are byte-identical to recent predictions. Four designs have newly high-confidence false pairs versus initial; the same cases recur in library mode.

cases.name: UCSolarCarTeam_Driver_Controls_Hardware
cases.classification: Wrong physical pad identity and new high-confidence propagation of that identity
cases.evidence: The PDF crop explicitly prints BOOT0 94 connected to GND and NRST 14 on the next line. The predicted pin at NRST's drawing position is numbered 94. The initial run left that wrong identity on an isolated NRST net; candidate joins it to the actual reset network, including C5 and R9, while source pad 94 belongs to ground. Passive alias swaps only determine which capacitor/resistor endpoint is reported; they cannot justify the MCU pad. This is an identity association error, not evidence that the reset and ground wire geometry crosses.

cases.name: ohdsp_DSP_ADAU1452_KiCad_DSP_ADAU1452_kicad_sch
cases.classification: Existing custom-diode pad reversal, promoted net confidence; explicit pin-guess warnings remain
cases.evidence: D306 uses custom DIODE pins 1=A and 2=K, rotated 180 degrees. CAD pad 2 is the cathode on the 2V1 output; prediction puts pad 2 at the anode on VDD. D307 has the complementary reversal on this network. The saved raw net membership is unchanged from initial. These new high-confidence false pairs arise from confidence promotion of an existing pad error; both diodes retain pin_number_guessed issues. No new geometric supply short is established.

cases.name: tzarc_keyboards_Ghoul_v1_0_ghoul_kicad_sch
cases.classification: Existing net-tie endpoint reversal, promoted net confidence; explicit pin-guess warning remains
cases.evidence: The source NetTie_2 at rotation 90 puts pad 2 at the upper +5V/Post endpoint and pad 1 on the lower feedback net. Prediction numbers the upper endpoint 1. Raw membership is identical to initial and the issue names both NT3 pads. A net tie intentionally bridges physical copper nets; this is a source pad-identity mismatch, not proof of a newly created unintended physical short.

cases.name: tzarc_keyboards_Kobold_R1_Kobold_kicad_sch
cases.classification: Existing bidirectional-TVS endpoint reversal, promoted net confidence; explicit pin-guess warning remains
cases.evidence: CAD D_TVS pins A1=1 and A2=2 at rotation 90 put pad 2 on VBUS_IN and pad 1 at GND. Prediction labels the upper VBUS_IN endpoint 1. The TVS is bidirectional, so this does not establish a new functional polarity fault; exact source pad identity differs. The frozen symmetric-passive allowlist does not reconcile TVS ends, and counts are retained. The pin-guess issue remains and raw membership is unchanged from initial.

adjudication.gate_assessment: Unsupported high-confidence pad identity criterion is not met versus initial, particularly U1.94. Absence of independent blinded review is an additional limitation; no positive blinded-review claim is made.
